Directional Flow Between Two Distributions

Source: R/dp-flux.R
dp_flux.Rd

Usage

dp_flux(
  resistance,
  origin,
  destination,
  radius = Inf,
  source_threshold = 0.01,
  radius_units = c("pixels", "km"),
  resistance_is = "resistances",
  normalize = TRUE,
  direction = TRUE,
  cell_value = c("absolute", "rms"),
  power = FALSE
)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface. Or a circuit from dp_circuit(), to reuse its factorization.

origin, destination

terra::SpatRasters or file paths on the same grid as resistance: origin and destination strength, e.g. habitat suitability in two periods or seasons. NA counts as 0.

radius

Numeric. The dispersal radius: origin and destination cells are paired if their centres are at most this far apart. In pixels by default (see radius_units). Default Inf, no distance limit.

source_threshold

Numeric. Cells with origin or destination strength below this are not origins or destinations. Default 0.01.

radius_units

Character. "pixels" (default): the radius counts cells, so the kernel is the cells with \(dr^2 + dc^2 \le\) radius\(^2\), as in os_run(). "km": great-circle distance between cell centres on lon/lat grids (the kernel narrows in degrees of longitude towards the poles), or distance in the coordinate reference system's units, converted to km, on projected grids.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances". Ignored for a circuit.

normalize

Logical. Also compute flow potential (the same flow on the uniform circuit, conductance 1 on the same cells) and normalized current. Default TRUE.

direction

Logical. Also return the components of net flow. Default TRUE.

cell_value

Character. How current sums a cell's links: "absolute" (default), half the sum of absolute current, as in Circuitscape's current maps; or "rms", the square root of half the sum of squared current, as in dp_omni().

power

Logical. Also map the power dissipated (see "Power" in dp_omni()), and with normalize, normalized power. Default FALSE.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers:

current

Half the sum of absolute current over a cell's links, as in Circuitscape's current maps, or with cell_value = "rms", the square root of half the sum of squared current. Unlike Circuitscape, it leaves out the current injected or withdrawn at the cell itself, so origin and destination cells read lower: a cell that injects one unit, all leaving along its links, has current 1/2 rather than 1.

flow_potential, normalized_current

(with normalize) current on the uniform circuit, summarised the same way, and current divided by it: above 1 where the landscape channels the flow, below 1 where it impedes it.

power, normalized_power

(with power; normalized_power also needs normalize) The power the flow dissipates: half the sum over a cell's links of squared current times the link's resistance, so cells sum to the total (see "Power" in dp_omni()); and power divided by the power on the uniform circuit.

flow_x, flow_y

(with direction) Net flow through the cell towards the east and the north, in grid directions: half the sum over the cell's links of the current along the link times its unit direction.

Three attributes say how much of the two distributions the map covers, each between 0 and 1:

"origin_in_reach"

The share of origin strength on cells with any destination strength within radius and in the same component. This is the one that says whether most of the origin has a destination within reach: origin cells without one send nothing. A cell that is both origin and destination counts as reached, although its pair with itself moves nothing.

"destination_in_reach"

The same for destination strength: the share on cells with any origin strength within reach.

"pair_weight_in_reach"

The share of all origin–destination pair weight, \(W / (\sum o \sum d)\), that is within radius and in the same component, and so carried by the map. It depends on the size of the domain relative to radius: where the distributions span many radii, most pairs are out of reach and the share is small, however closely the two distributions overlap. With radius = Inf and one component, it is 1.

Details

Maps the net flow from an origin distribution to a destination distribution, with its direction, in one solve: for example from present to future habitat, from breeding to wintering grounds, or from source populations to restoration sites. Flows in opposite directions cancel, so the map shows net movement. For movement between the two distributions without direction, where every pair counts whichever way it flows, see dp_omni() with a destination.

Current flows along the circuit's links: the resistors joining each cell to its 8 neighbours (see dp_circuit()). The map is defined per link, as the signed sum over origin–destination pairs of cells within radius of each other, $$F_e = \frac{1}{W} \sum_{i,j} o_i\, d_j\, k(d_{ij})\, I_e(i,j),$$ where \(o\) and \(d\) are origin and destination strength, \(k\) is 1 for cells within radius of each other and 0 otherwise, \(I_e(i,j)\) is the current through link \(e\) when one unit flows from \(i\) to \(j\), and \(W = \sum_{i,j} o_i d_j k(d_{ij})\) makes the pair weights sum to one unit of flow. Pairs never span groups of cells that NA cells separate (components), since no current passes between them. A cell's value combines the links that meet at it, up to 8 (see current below), each link being shared by the two cells it joins.

The sum is linear in the pairs' currents, so it takes a single solve, of the injection \(b_i = (o_i\, (Kd)_i - d_i\, (Ko)_i) / W\), where \((Kd)_i\) is the destination strength within reach of cell \(i\) and \((Ko)_i\) the origin strength within reach of it. Each origin cell sends flow in proportion to its strength and the destination strength within its reach; each destination cell receives in proportion to its strength and the origin strength within its reach. A cell's pair with itself counts in \(W\) but moves nothing, so where origin and destination overlap, flow cancels.

With radius = Inf and one component, this is the injection \(b = o / \sum o - d / \sum d\): one unit enters at the origin and leaves at the destination, wherever it has to travel. That is the minimum-energy flow that turns the origin distribution into the destination one.

Withdrawals are fixed, not grounds: each destination cell takes its share however electrically far away it is. (With grounds, as in cs_advanced(), current drains into the nearest destination instead.)

Swapping origin and destination reverses the flow: the same current, with flow_x and flow_y negated.

Directional and undirected maps

dp_omni() with a destination maps the undirected counterpart, from the same pairs: their squared currents, so flows in opposite directions don't cancel. dp_directionality() computes both maps at once, with their ratio, which shows where movement between the two distributions is one-way and where it runs both ways.

Performance

The time is mostly factoring the circuit, and with normalize, its uniform twin, which about doubles it; set normalize = FALSE to skip that. Each map then takes one solve. To reuse factorizations across runs, pass a circuit from dp_circuit().

See also

dp_omni(), dp_directionality(), cs_advanced()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available(circuitscape = FALSE)
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
origin <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/source.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
destination <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/ground.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
result <- dp_flux(resistance, origin, destination)
terra::plot(result)

# Only pairs within 45 cells of each other
near <- dp_flux(resistance, origin, destination, radius = 45)
attr(near, "origin_in_reach")
attr(near, "pair_weight_in_reach")
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
